summary: Off-LAN camera control in the Tapo app. Every camera JSON command is the LAN request wrapped in multipleRequest. For cameras in the IoT thing list (all current Tapo cameras) it is sent as POST {thing appServerUrlV2||appServerUrl}/v1/things/{deviceId}/services-sync with body {serviceId:'passthrough',inputParams:{requestData:<object>}} and IoT headers (Authorization ut|token, no signing). The reply is outputParams.responseData = {error_code,result:{responses[]}}. The legacy signed POST {appServerUrl}/api/v2/common/passthrough?token=.. {requestData,deviceId} is used only when the camera has no thing record. The app routes LOCAL -> REMOTE -> IOT_REMOTE, and LOCAL is enabled only for the owner (TDP owner hash), so shared users always go through the cloud with their own token and the same body. No MQTT path carries commands. Remote SD playback/download uses the same CIPC /v2/relay/request with streamType 1 (playback) / 3 (+subType cover|video) and channelId '0', customParams JSON string (event_type etc.), then the tunnel carries the LAN 'get playback'/'get download' JSON parts, acks every 25 parts, heartbeats, and ends on stream_status finished. Talkback uses streamType 2 / type=dtspk with customParams mode half_duplex|aec.

items.description: How the app picks the transport for every camera JSON command (getDeviceInfo, motorMove, setLedStatus, searchVideoWithUTC, ...). TPCameraClient.yj() builds up to four transports per camera; routing hf(null) tries them in a fixed order. There is no per-command choice: every command goes through the first ready transport.

value.LOCAL: enabled only if the TDP discovery record exists AND tdp.owner equalsIgnoreCase md5_hex(account localUserName). Shared users therefore never get a LAN transport in the app.
value.REMOTE (legacy): enabled only if the legacy cloud device (TCDeviceBean from the old device list) has appServerUrl(V2) AND the camera has NO IoT thing record (getMThingDevice()==null).
value.IOT_REMOTE: enabled if the camera has a thing record with thingUrlRenewal (thingInfo.appServerUrlV2 || appServerUrl) and a non-empty deviceId.
value.effect: Because REMOTE is switched off whenever a thing record exists, a current Tapo camera (isSupportIoTCloud) always uses IOT_REMOTE off-LAN. The legacy passthrough is only for old accounts or devices that are not in the IoT thing list.
value.transport_wait_timeout: getting a transport times out after 30 s (Pc(): E1(30, SECONDS))
value.failure_retry: on a failure the client re-initialises IOT_REMOTE first (log 'retry iot remote'), else REMOTE ('retry remote'), then retries

getMThingDevice() == null || getThingUrlRenewal() == null -> disable IOT_REMOTE

items.description: What runs inside the relay tunnel for playback/download. The stream-control layer (f51.k0) is transport-agnostic: once the relay tunnel is up it is used exactly like the LAN :8800 /stream session, without the inner POST /stream and without Digest/Key-Exchange (as for preview).

value.first_part: {"type":"request","seq":1,"params":{"method":"get","playback":{"client_id":<int>,"scale":"1/1","start_time":"<utc s>","end_time":"<utc s>","event_type":[..],"filter":true}}}. The app sets only client_id, scale, start_time, end_time (optional), event_type+filter, face_id, det_origin, play_channel, audio_config, data_filter_tag; it does NOT set player_id or channels here.
value.start_time_rule: start_time must be > 0 or the app refuses; end_time only if > 0; filter=true only if event_type non-empty
value.player_id: no separate player_id is required in the JSON: the relay slot is already bound to playerId/bidirectionid by the relay request
value.acks: same flow-control acks as LAN: every 25th received part (X-Data-Sequence % 25 == 0) send a JSON part with X-Data-Received/X-Session-Id
value.end_of_clip: device notification stream_status 'finished' (vod.stream.notifications); also socket close by the relay
value.data_timeout: native connection timeout passed to the stream engine: 5000 ms for LAN (connection type 16), 18000 ms for relay/other types
value.encryption: no Key-Exchange on relay; treat payload as plaintext TS (see remote_spec unresolved)

items.description: What changes for a shared camera (role 1) or a camera without localAccessToken.

value.transport: LOCAL is disabled (TDP owner = md5(owner's localUserName) never matches the shared account), so every command goes through IOT_REMOTE services-sync with the SHARED user's own ut|<token>. Request body is identical (no familyId, no role, no owner fields).
value.lat: owner-only operations (changeAdminPassword LAT sync, needSyncDevicePasswordV3) are skipped when !isOwner()
value.relay_cipc: /v2/relay/request body has no role/share field; Authorization is the shared user's own account token. relayToken from the reply goes into X-token as usual.
value.native_relay_token_suffix: the native relay/P2P client path (ub1.d) builds its account-token credential with a suffix: owner camera -> '<token>', shared (role 1) -> '<token>; tokenType=appSlaveToken', owner sub-device -> '; tokenType=appSubDeviceToken', shared sub-device -> '; tokenType=appSlaveSubDeviceToken'. Used only when no relayToken is supplied.
value.ui_gating: the app hides owner-only UI with isOwner()/isUserRoleTypeDevice(): device settings page (DeviceSettingViewModelV2 owner flag), smart actions/automation filters exclude shared cameras, contacts/one-touch-call/growth-record/splendid-moment owner checks, hub sensor binding. The cloud/camera enforces the actual permission; a rejected command comes back as a cloud or inner error_code.
value.allowed_for_shared_users_by_app: live view, playback/download, PTZ, talk and basic toggles are reachable; settings/management and sharing are owner-only (inferred from UI gating)

items.description: Desktop-client recipe for sending camera JSON commands when the camera is not on the LAN (or the account is a shared user).

steps: 1. Sign in (TP-Link ID, signed /api/v2) and keep the account token; refresh it on HTTP 401 / -20651.
2. Load the IoT thing list (/v2/things ... with Authorization: ut|<token>). For the camera keep thingName, appServerUrlV2 (fallback appServerUrl), role, shareType, localAccessToken.

3. Choose the path: if the camera is in the thing list with a thing URL -> IoT path (step 4). Only if it is missing there but present in the legacy device list with appServerUrl -> legacy path (step 7).

4. Build the inner request exactly as on LAN and wrap it: {"method":"multipleRequest","params":{"requests":[{"method":"motorMove","params":{"motor":{"move":{"x_coord":"10","y_coord":"0"}}}}]}}. Several commands may go in one requests[] list.

5. POST {thingUrl}/v1/things/{thingName}/services-sync with the IoT headers (Authorization: ut|<token>, app-cid, x-app-name, x-app-version, x-term-id, x-ospf, x-net-type, x-strict: 0, x-locale, Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8) and body {"serviceId":"passthrough","inputParams":{"requestData":<object from step 4>}}. Use a 30 s timeout.

6. On HTTP 200 read outputParams; if it has 'responseData' use that, else outputParams itself. Check its error_code == 0, then match result.responses[i] to requests[i] (each has method, result, error_code). On non-2xx parse {code,message} and the HTTP status; on 429 back off.

7. Legacy path: POST {appServerUrl}/api/v2/common/passthrough?token=<token>&appName=..&termID=..&ospf=..&appVer=..&netType=..&locale=.. signed like other /api/v2 calls, body {"requestData":<object from step 4>,"deviceId":"<deviceId>"}. Read result.responseData (camera reply) after checking outer error_code (-20571 offline, -20002 camera timeout, -20651 token expired).
8. Serialise requests per camera; treat a missing/zero-length responses[] as failure; retry once after re-fetching the thing list if the thing URL changed.

items.description: Desktop-client recipe for remote SD playback and clip download through the CIPC relay.

steps: 1. Find recordings with the control path above: searchDateWithVideo, then searchVideoWithUTC (multipleRequest through services-sync), same params as LAN (sd_vod_playback_spec).
2. Resolve the CIPC host (getAppServiceUrl serviceIds ['cipc.api.cloud']) as for live view.

3. POST https://<cipcHost>/v2/relay/request (Authorization: <raw account token>, X-Request-Signature: 10 random chars, User-Agent) with body {"deviceId":id,"dataTimeoutCount":0,"cloudType":2,"deviceType":"SMART.IPCAMERA","playerId":uuid,"rootCaVer":"1","streamType":1,"channelId":"0","customParams":"{}","trackId":uuid}. customParams may carry {"event_type":[..]} to filter. For download use streamType 3, subType "cover" (clip download) and channelId "0".

4. From result take relayUrl (path has type=sdvod&playerid=.. or type=download&bidirectionid=..), relayIp, relayToken; open TLS to relayIp:443 (SNI relay host) and send 'POST <relayPath>&retryTime=0 HTTP/1.1' with the relay headers (X-token: relayToken, Keep-Relay: 3600, Content-Type multipart/mixed;boundary=--client-stream-boundary--, X-Version: 2.0, X-Pull-Mode: 2, ...). Wait for HTTP 200.

5. Do NOT send an inner 'POST /stream' or Digest. Immediately write the JSON part: {"type":"request","seq":1,"params":{"method":"get","playback":{"client_id":<int>,"scale":"1/1","start_time":"<utc s>","end_time":"<utc s>"}}} (start_time > 0 required). For download: {"method":"get","download":{...}} as on LAN.

6. Read device parts (boundary ----device-stream-boundary--): first the JSON response with error_code 0 and session_id; then video/mp2t parts with X-Data-Sequence/X-Data-PTS. Every 25th part send the ack part (X-Data-Received, X-Session-Id). Send the heartbeat notification every 15 s.
7. Seek/speed/pause with 'do' control parts carrying the session_id, exactly as on LAN.

8. The clip/range ends on a notification with event_type stream_status and status 'finished'; also stop on tunnel close or 18 s without data. Open a new relay slot (new trackId/playerId) for every new session; relay errors -52407 (too many clients), -52212 (flow limit), -100001 (relay request limit), -1007 (offline) are fatal for the attempt.

unresolved.detail: The APK never names the IoT-cloud code for 'camera offline' or 'camera did not answer' on services-sync; errors arrive as HTTP 4xx/5xx with {code,message}. Capture them live (expect something analogous to legacy -20571/-20002).
No permission matrix is in the APK. The app only hides owner-only UI by role; which inner methods the cloud/camera rejects for role 1 must be tested live.
Most paths expect outputParams.responseData; one path parses outputParams directly. Confirm on a live camera which shape the cloud returns (handle both).
No client rate limiter for passthrough; HTTP 429 handling exists for edge hosts only. Real limits are unknown.
REA android class/method inspection is unavailable (REA_JADX_MCP_JAR not configured); evidence is from JADX sources via ripgrep plus one REA inspect-artifact run.
